title: Turn your project into a case study
summary: A short, honest case study shows how you think, which matters more than polished screens. It is also what you will talk through in interviews.

beginner: Outline the story in six parts: the context, the problem, how you learned, what you decided and why, what happened, and what you would do differently.
Write each part in plain language in a sentence or two, then expand. Keep the whole piece to one or two pages.
Show your evidence: a quote from an interview, a table of your scores or your one-page brief. Remove names and personal details.
Be explicit about your own role and what you would do differently. Honest limits make a case study more credible.
If any part used work material, remove it. Do not name employers, clients or colleagues, or share internal documents or numbers.
Publish it somewhere you control, such as a simple page or a shared document, and write a three-sentence summary you can say aloud.
Ask one person to read it and tell you what is unclear.

toolExamples.google-docs: Write it as a shared document and turn on link sharing only when you are ready.
toolExamples.notion: Publish a simple page with the six headings.

definitionOfDone: A one-to-two page case study with the six parts
Evidence included, with no confidential or personal information
pitfalls: Showing only the result and not the thinking
Claiming credit for work you did not do
